newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker says Medicare program wastes millions.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker says Medicare program wastes millions.

text.p: A key Republican Wednesday charged the Clinton administration had wasted $65 million in a failed effort to develop a computer system to weed out fraud in the Medicare program, vowing a full investigation.

"This program is out of control, out of balance and doesn't even work," said Caifornia Republican Rep. Bill Thomas, releasing administration documents that he said outlined tens of millions of dollars in cost overruns.

Federal officials last month quietly stopped work on much of the so-called Medicare Transaction System for 90 days. The project was supposed to consolidate 72 different payment methods into one centrally run system, making Medicare more efficient and preventing fraud and abuse.
Admitting some mistakes had been made, officials said they still hoped to salvage the new data system. They also said cost overruns were almost inevitable on a project so large.
The project started in 1994, when the agency awarded a contract to GTE Government Services.
Thomas released HCFA documents showing the project had racked up a cost overrun of $65.3 million as of March. Total spending was $101.9 million, compared to an original budget of $36.6 million.
Earlier this month, HCFA announced it had imposed a 90-day stop order on most of the project, with the exception of provisions dealing with managed care.
